2: 
3: You're here to play the mmo game through the progressive development of botting scripts, starting small then adapting to your desires and ideas.
4: It is strongly recommended to get started and make the first step towards your goals, then researching and learning as you go.
5: 
6: ## First Time Setup
7: 
8: **Create a new bot using the setup script:**
9: 
10: Ask the user for a bot name (max 12 chars, alphanumeric). If they skip, use the command without a username to auto-generate a random 9-character name.
11: 
12: ```bash
13: # With custom username
14: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username}
15: 
16: # Auto-generate random username
17: bun bots/create-bot.ts
18: 
19: # Use local server (sets SERVER=localhost in bot.env)
20: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --local
21: 
22: # Use a custom server
23: bun bots/create-bot.ts {username} --server=myserver.example.com
24: ```
25: 
26: This automatically creates:
27: 
28: - `bots/{username}/bot.env` - Credentials with auto-generated password
29: - `bots/{username}/lab_log.md` - Session notes template
30: - `bots/{username}/script.ts` - Ready-to-run starter script
31: 
32: ### Start a Game Client (scripts only)
33: 
34: Scripts (`bun bots/{username}/*.ts`) and `bun sdk/cli.ts` need a running game
35: client; they never start one. Before running a script, start the headless lite
36: client in the background and leave it running:
37: 
38: ```bash
39: cd server/webclient && bun install && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}
40: ```
41: 
42: It logs `Gateway connected, registering as '{username}'` once it's ready. One
43: process per bot; it exits non-zero if the game session ends. Without it, a
44: script exits with `No game client is attached`. MCP `execute_code` doesn't need
45: this step; it opens a browser client itself.
46: 
47: ### Quick Start
48: 
49: 1. Install dependencies: `bun install` (from project root)
50: 2. Open project in your AI coding tool — the MCP server will be available automatically
51: 3. Control your bot with suggestions.
52: 
53: ### Tools
54: 
55: | Tool                           | Description                                    |
56: | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
57: | `execute_code(bot_name, code)` | Run code on a bot. Auto-connects on first use. |
58: | `list_bots()`                  | List connected bots                            |
59: | `disconnect_bot(name)`         | Disconnect a bot                               |
60: 
61: ### Example
62: 
63: ```typescript
64: // Just execute - auto-connects on first use
65: execute_code({
66:   bot_name: "mybot",
67:   code: `
68:     const state = sdk.getState();
69:     console.log('Position:', state.player.worldX, state.player.worldZ);
70: 
71:     // Chop trees for 1 minute
72:     const endTime = Date.now() + 60_000;
73:     while (Date.now() < endTime) {
74:       const tree = sdk.findNearbyLoc(/^tree$/i);
75:       if (tree) await bot.chopTree(tree);
76:     }
77: 
78:     return sdk.getInventory();
79:   `,
80: });
81: ```
82: 
83: See `mcp/README.md` for detailed API reference.
84: 
85: Code runs in an async context with `bot` (BotActions) and `sdk` (BotSDK) available as globals.
86: 
87: ## Reporting SDK Bugs
88: 
89: When the SDK has a bug or rough edge, first find a workaround, then file a report. One command, no auth, no permission needed:
90: 
91: ```bash
92: bun sdk/bug-report.ts "incorrect results from bot.foo(), had to use raw sdk.sendFoo() instead for xyz reason."
93: ```
94: 
95: Important note: The game itself is extremely well tested and complete, it's not buggy. If you can't figure out how to do something, don't blame the game, blame your assumptions and keep investigating. File a bug report _after_ you figure out
96: what's going on, don't just assume the game is broken because you got confused, and give up. The SDK is a thin layer on top of the game, and the game is the source of truth.
97: 
98: After filing the bug, keep working on your goal!
99: 
100: ## Session Workflow
101: 
102: This is a **persistent character** - you don't restart fresh each time. The workflow is:
103: 
104: ### 1. Check World State First
105: 
106: Before writing any script, check where the bot is and what it has:
107: 
108: ```bash
109: bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
110: ```
111: 
112: This shows: position, inventory, skills, nearby NPCs/objects, and more.
113: 
114: **Exception**: Skip this if you just created the character and know it's at spawn.
115: 
116: **Tutorial Check**: If the character is in the tutorial area, call `await bot.skipTutorial()` before running any other scripts. The tutorial blocks normal gameplay.
117: 
118: ### 2. Write Your Script
119: 
120: Edit `bots/{username}/script_name.ts` with your goal. Keep scripts focused on one task. you may write multiple scripts for different tasks and switch between them.
121: 
122: ### 3. Run the Script
123: 
124: ```bash
125: bun bots/{username}/script_name.ts
126: ```
127: 
128: ### 4. Observe and Iterate
129: 
130: Watch the output. After the script finishes (or fails), check state again:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: bun sdk/cli.ts {username}
134: ```
135: 
136: Record observations in `lab_log.md`, then improve the script.
137: 
138: ### Chatting Without Taking Control
139: 
140: To talk in-game (or read chat) without disturbing whatever script currently
141: owns the bot, use the chat CLI — it connects in `observe` mode, which can send
142: chat (and nothing else) and never pre-empts (or gets pre-empted by) a
143: controller:
144: 
145: ```bash
146: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} "meet me at the bank"   # send public chat
147: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --to {player} "on my way"  # send a private message
148: bun sdk/chat.ts {username}                          # recent chat
149: bun sdk/chat.ts {username} --watch                  # tail live
150: ```
151: 
152: Public chat is capped at 400 chars per message; `sdk.say()` auto-splits longer
153: text into wire-safe chunks.
154: 
155: Private messages (`sdk.dm(name, text)` / `sdk.sendPrivateMessage(name, msg)`)
156: reach the target anywhere in the world - no friends-list setup needed - and
157: show up in `getChat()` as type 3 (received) / 6 (sent). The server accepts one
158: social packet (say or PM) per tick; `dm()` paces its chunks automatically.
159: 
160: ## Script Duration Guidelines
161: 
162: **Start short, extend as you gain confidence:**
163: 
164: | Duration      | Use When                                              |
165: | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
166: | **10s**       | New script, single actions, untested logic, debugging |
167: | **30s-1 min** | Validated approach, building confidence               |
168: | **5+ min**    | Proven strategy, grinding runs. USE SPARINGLY         |
169: 
170: A failed 5-minute run wastes more time than five 30 second diagnostic runs. **Fail fast and start simple.**
171: 
172: Look out for "I can't reach" messages - the solution is often to open closed gates or that the item isn't accessible.
173: 
174: Read and grep in the learnings/ and wiki/ folder for tips, skill guides, item and npc locations, and shop information.

176: ## SDK API Reference

180: **Quick overview:**
181: 
182: - `bot.*` - High-level actions that attempt to observe method-specific evidence (chopTree, walkTo, attack, etc.). Check a result when the method returns one.

186: 
187: | Method                          | What it does                                                     |
188: | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |

190: | `talkTo(target)`                | Walk to NPC, start dialog                                        |
191: | `interactNpc(target, option?)`  | Walk to NPC, interact with any option (e.g. `'trade'`, `'fish'`) |
192: | `interactLoc(target, option?)`  | Walk to loc, interact with any option (e.g. `'mine'`, `'smelt'`) |
193: | `attack(target)`                | Walk to an NPC or player and start combat                    |
194: | `castSpell(target, spell)`      | Cast a combat spell on an NPC or player                         |
195: | `pickpocketNpc(target)`         | Pickpocket NPC, detects XP gain vs stun                          |
196: | `chopTree(target?)`             | Chop tree, wait for logs                                         |
197: | `pickupItem(target)`            | Pick up ground item                                              |
198: | `openDoor(target?)`             | Open a door or gate                                              |
199: | `openBank()`                    | Open nearest bank                                                |
200: | `depositItem(target, amount?)`  | Deposit item to bank                                             |
201: | `withdrawItem(slot, amount?)`   | Withdraw item from bank                                          |
202: | `closeInterface()`              | Close any open modal (shop, bank, book, quest scroll)            |
203: | `closeShop()` / `closeBank()`   | Close the shop / bank interface                                  |
204: | `openShop(target?)`             | Open shop via shopkeeper NPC                                     |
205: | `buyFromShop(target, amount?)`  | Buy item from open shop                                          |
206: | `sellToShop(target, amount?)`   | Sell item to open shop                                           |
207: | `equipItem(target)`             | Equip from inventory                                             |
208: | `unequipItem(target)`           | Unequip to inventory                                             |
209: | `eatFood(target)`               | Eat food, returns HP gained                                      |
210: | `useItemOnLoc(item, loc)`       | Use inventory item on loc (e.g. fish on range)                   |
211: | `useItemOnNpc(item, npc)`       | Use inventory item on NPC                                        |
212: | `burnLogs(target?)`             | Light logs with tinderbox                                        |
213: | `fletchLogs(product?)`          | Fletch logs with knife                                           |
214: | `craftLeather(product?)`        | Craft leather with needle                                        |
215: | `smithAtAnvil(product)`         | Smith bars at anvil                                              |
216: | `dismissBlockingUI()`           | Dismiss level-up dialogs (called automatically by all actions)   |
217: | `navigateDialog(choices)`       | Auto-click through dialog options                                |
218: | `skipTutorial()`                | Skip the tutorial island                                         |
219: 
220: ### sdk.\* Commonly Used Directly
221: 
222: | Method                                              | What it does                                        |
223: | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
224: | `getState()`                                        | Full world state snapshot                           |
225: | `getSkill(name)` / `getSkillXp(name)`               | Skill info                                          |
226: | `getInventory()` / `findInventoryItem(pattern)`     | Inventory queries                                   |
227: | `findNearbyNpc(pattern)` / `findNearbyLoc(pattern)` | Find nearby entities                                |
228: | `findNearbyPlayer(pattern)` / `getNearbyPlayers()`  | Find other players                                  |
229: | `findGroundItem(pattern)`                           | Find ground items                                   |
230: | `getDialog()`                                       | Current dialog state                                |
231: | `sendClickDialog(option)`                           | Click dialog option by its published `index`        |
232: | `clickDialogByText(pattern)`                        | Click dialog option by label — prefer this          |
233: | `sendClickComponent(id)`                            | Click interface button                              |
234: | `sendCloseModal()` / `sendCloseShop()`              | Close the open modal / shop                         |
235: | `sendDropItem(slot)`                                | Drop inventory item                                 |
236: | `sendUseItem(slot)`                                 | Use inventory item (bury, etc.)                     |
237: | `sendUseItemOnItem(src, dst)`                       | Combine two items                                   |
238: | `say(text)`                                         | Send chat, auto-chunked past the length cap         |
239: | `dm(name, text)`                                    | Send a private message, auto-chunked                |
240: | `getChat(opts?)` / `getNewChat(opts?)`              | Read chat history (500-deep) / only unseen messages |
241: | `waitForChat(opts?)`                                | Wait for a message (`{from, matching, timeout}`)    |
242: | `waitForCondition(pred)`                            | Wait for state predicate                            |
243: | `waitForTicks(n)`                                   | Wait n game ticks                                   |
244: | `scanNearbyLocs(radius?)`                           | Async extended-range loc scan; must be awaited      |
245: 
246: See `sdk/API.md` for exact async signatures, parameter defaults, and return
247: types.
248: 
249: ### Code environments
250: 
251: MCP `execute_code` exposes `bot` and `sdk` directly. Standalone
252: `bots/{username}/*.ts` files must import `runScript` and receive
253: `{ bot, sdk }` in its callback. Do not paste runner-context expressions into
254: `execute_code`.
255: 
256: Only one control connection should own a bot. Use observe mode for read-only
257: monitoring, avoid overlapping action programs on the same bot, and inspect
258: `sdk.getStateAge()` before acting after a disconnect or long pause.
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ### Modals Hide the Inventory
263: 
264: A shop or bank modal replaces the inventory tab, so the server rejects
265: inventory packets sent underneath it as "component not visible" — with no game
266: message. Close the modal before doing anything else:
267: 
268: ```typescript
269: await bot.closeInterface(); // any modal
270: await bot.closeShop(); // shop specifically
271: await sdk.sendCloseModal(); // low-level
272: ```
273: 
274: Don't click the interface's own "Close Window" component id. It's a
275: client-side close button with no server trigger; the SDK now routes those to a
276: close for you, but the named methods above are what to reach for.
277: 
278: ### Dialog Options Are Not In Product Order
279: 
280: Skill dialogs (fletching, crafting) publish four buttons _per product_ — Make
281: X, Make 10, Make 5, then one labelled with the product name. Arrow shafts are
282: option 4 of 12, not option 1. Never assume ordering:
283: 
284: ```typescript
285: const dialog = sdk.getDialog();
286: console.log(dialog?.options.map((o) => `${o.index}: ${o.text}`));
287: await sdk.clickDialogByText(/arrow shaft/i); // or bot.fletchLogs('arrow shaft')
288: ```
289: 
290: ### Dismiss Level-Up Dialogs
291: 
292: All BotActions methods automatically dismiss blocking UI (level-up dialogs, etc.) before executing. You don't need to call this manually in loops.
293: 
294: ```typescript
295: // Only needed if using low-level sdk methods directly:
296: await bot.dismissBlockingUI();
297: 
298: // Or manually check
299: if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
300:   await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
301: }
302: ```
303: 
304: ### Error Handling
305: 
306: ```typescript
307: const result = await bot.chopTree();
308: if (!result.success) {
309:   console.log(`Failed: ${result.message}`);
310:   // Handle failure - maybe walk somewhere else
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ## Project Structure
315: 
316: ```
317: 
318: bots/
319: └── {username}/
320:     ├── bot.env        # Credentials (BOT_USERNAME, PASSWORD, SERVER)
321:     ├── lab_log.md     # Session notes and observations
322:     └── script.ts      # Current script
323: 
324: sdk/
325: ├── index.ts           # BotSDK (low-level)
326: ├── actions.ts         # BotActions (high-level)
327: ├── cli.ts             # CLI for checking state
328: └── types.ts           # Type definitions
329: 
330: learnings/
331: ├── banking.md
332: └── ...etc
333: 
334: wiki/
335: ├── npcs/
336: ├── items/
337: ├── skills/
338: └── shops/
339: 
340: ```
341: 
342: ## Troubleshooting
343: 
344: **"No game client is attached" / "No state received"** - No client is publishing state for the bot. Start the lite client (`cd server/webclient && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}`) or open the bot's browser URL, then rerun.
345: 
346: **"Client out of date" / "the server now runs revision N" / lite runner exits with code 3** - The game server was upgraded to a new game revision. Update your checkout (`git pull`, then `cd server/webclient && bun install`) and restart the lite runner. Browser clients only need a page reload.
347: 
348: **Script stalls** - Check for open dialogs (`state.dialog.isOpen`). Level-ups block everything.
349: 
350: **"Can't reach"** - Path is blocked. Try walking closer first, or find a different target.
351: 
352: **Wrong target** - Use more specific regex patterns: `/^tree$/i` not `/tree/i` (which matches "tree stump").
353: 
354: **Everything succeeds and nothing happens** - The two silent failure modes. A
355: `send*` returning success only means the client wrote bytes; it is not an ack.
356: 
357: - **The client never sent anything.** The client pathfinds before every interaction, and when it can't route it returns `cant_reach` without writing a packet - so the server never replies "I can't reach that!" either. Check `reachable` on the target before using it. `find*` already prefers reachable matches; pass `{reachable: true}` to get `null` instead of an unreachable one.
358: - **The server discarded the op.** A refused op (mid-action, stunned, target gone or out of view, bad option) gets `UNSET_MAP_FLAG` and nothing else - no message, no error. A blocking modal is worse: the op is accepted and the trigger never runs. Check `state.opFeedback.opRejectedCount` around a send, and gate loops on an observed effect rather than on a timer.
359: 
360: Start small and build up!

### Code environments

MCP `execute_code` exposes `bot` and `sdk` directly. Standalone
`bots/{username}/*.ts` files must import `runScript` and receive
`{ bot, sdk }` in its callback. Do not paste runner-context expressions into
`execute_code`.

Only one control connection should own a bot. Use observe mode for read-only
monitoring, avoid overlapping action programs on the same bot, and inspect
`sdk.getStateAge()` before acting after a disconnect or long pause.

---

### Modals Hide the Inventory

A shop or bank modal replaces the inventory tab, so the server rejects
inventory packets sent underneath it as "component not visible" — with no game
message. Close the modal before doing anything else:

```typescript
await bot.closeInterface(); // any modal
await bot.closeShop(); // shop specifically
await sdk.sendCloseModal(); // low-level
```

Don't click the interface's own "Close Window" component id. It's a
client-side close button with no server trigger; the SDK now routes those to a
close for you, but the named methods above are what to reach for.

### Dialog Options Are Not In Product Order

Skill dialogs (fletching, crafting) publish four buttons _per product_ — Make
X, Make 10, Make 5, then one labelled with the product name. Arrow shafts are
option 4 of 12, not option 1. Never assume ordering:

```typescript
const dialog = sdk.getDialog();
console.log(dialog?.options.map((o) => `${o.index}: ${o.text}`));
await sdk.clickDialogByText(/arrow shaft/i); // or bot.fletchLogs('arrow shaft')
```

### Dismiss Level-Up Dialogs

All BotActions methods automatically dismiss blocking UI (level-up dialogs, etc.) before executing. You don't need to call this manually in loops.

```typescript
// Only needed if using low-level sdk methods directly:
await bot.dismissBlockingUI();

// Or manually check
if (sdk.getState()?.dialog.isOpen) {
  await sdk.sendClickDialog(0);
}
```

```typescript
const result = await bot.chopTree();
if (!result.success) {
  console.log(`Failed: ${result.message}`);
  // Handle failure - maybe walk somewhere else
}
```

## Troubleshooting

**"No game client is attached" / "No state received"** - No client is publishing state for the bot. Start the lite client (`cd server/webclient && bun src/lite/runner.ts {username}`) or open the bot's browser URL, then rerun.

**"Client out of date" / "the server now runs revision N" / lite runner exits with code 3** - The game server was upgraded to a new game revision. Update your checkout (`git pull`, then `cd server/webclient && bun install`) and restart the lite runner. Browser clients only need a page reload.

**Script stalls** - Check for open dialogs (`state.dialog.isOpen`). Level-ups block everything.

**"Can't reach"** - Path is blocked. Try walking closer first, or find a different target.

**Wrong target** - Use more specific regex patterns: `/^tree$/i` not `/tree/i` (which matches "tree stump").

**Everything succeeds and nothing happens** - The two silent failure modes. A
`send*` returning success only means the client wrote bytes; it is not an ack.

- **The client never sent anything.** The client pathfinds before every interaction, and when it can't route it returns `cant_reach` without writing a packet - so the server never replies "I can't reach that!" either. Check `reachable` on the target before using it. `find*` already prefers reachable matches; pass `{reachable: true}` to get `null` instead of an unreachable one.
- **The server discarded the op.** A refused op (mid-action, stunned, target gone or out of view, bad option) gets `UNSET_MAP_FLAG` and nothing else - no message, no error. A blocking modal is worse: the op is accepted and the trigger never runs. Check `state.opFeedback.opRejectedCount` around a send, and gate loops on an observed effect rather than on a timer.

Start small and build up!
